acceptanceCriteria: repository-state-unstable, dogfood-event-repository-drift and dogfood-event-context-drift surface to the adapter as one fixed bounded code (for example dogfood-event-worktree-churn) and dogfood-event-policy-drift passes through; other causes stay dogfood-event-unavailable; no caller data enters the code (LCP-V0-008 amended).
The repository-state-unstable message names what changed (HEAD, or the dirty set) instead of always saying HEAD changed.
Maintained tests drive each mapped cause and assert the surfaced code, and an unlisted error still maps to dogfood-event-unavailable.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

Found by the V1-0870 lane (2026-10-06) while diagnosing the FALLBACK warning corvint-event-rejected:dogfood-event-unavailable seen on the primary at load 16.8/32.2/45.0. cmd/corvint/local_completion_event.go (about line 152) maps every non-allowlisted error from dogfoodEventWithin to the fixed code dogfood-event-unavailable. A private reproduction with untracked files churning every 15 ms returned dogfood-event-context-drift three times and repository-state-unstable once; quiet runs succeeded. The inferred cause on the primary is concurrent writes (for example .taskman/tickets) growing the dirty set (2283 then 2592 paths) between the event's two repository probes; not confirmed. internal/gokernel/repository.go (about line 386) words repository-state-unstable as 'repository HEAD changed' even when only the dirty set changed. A snapshot evicted mid-read is not a cause: it surfaces as dogfood-event-index-snapshot-stale.
title: Dogfood events report worktree churn as the opaque dogfood-event-unavailable, and repository-state-unstable says HEAD changed when only the dirty set did
